steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Technical skills are the specific physical competences that enable a dancer to perform movement accurately and safely

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Posture is the way the body is held and provides the base from which all movement begins

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Alignment refers to the correct positioning of body parts in relation to one another, ensuring efficient movement

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Control is the ability to manage the body's movement with precision, including speed, direction and dynamics

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between posture and alignment? | Q: Why is spatial awareness important in group dance? | Q: How does control affect the quality of a slow, sustained movement?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Posture is the overall way the body is held; alignment is the specific positioning of body parts in relation to each other for efficient movement. | Spatial awareness allows dancers to maintain correct formations, avoid collisions, use the performance space effectively and ensure the audience can see the choreography. | Control enables the dancer to move with even speed and steady dynamics, creating a smooth, continuous line without wobbling or losing balance.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Distinguish clearly between posture (how the body is held overall) and alignment (how body parts relate to each other) When writing about control, always link it to a specific movement quality such as sustained or sudden dynamics Spatial awareness questions often require you to discuss formations, levels, directions and use of stage area Use dance terminology rather than everyday language — say 'alignment' not 'standing up straight' In performance analysis, mention at least two technical skills and connect them to the choreographic intention
